claim: Unmonitored commitment to an approach (wild goose chase) is a main cause of failure in human novice problem solving; experts interrupt and re-plan.
agent_test: Log commit points; count tokens spent after first commit without a progress check; compare with a forced progress check every N tokens.

claim: Control decisions are needed at three loci: episode junctions, arrival of new information, and a run of tactical failures; the third (stall detection) is hard to code.
agent_test: Implement the three triggers as separate S6 rules and ablate each at equal tokens.

claim: Without external or oracle feedback, intrinsic self-correction by prompted LLMs does not help and often lowers reasoning accuracy (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7; CommonsenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0).
agent_test: Compare blind re-read of own answer vs none at equal tokens; require an external check (code run, tool, independent sample) for any revision.

claim: The apparent gains of self-correction in earlier papers came from oracle correctness labels that told the model when to stop; a real agent lacks this.
agent_test: Re-run any reflect-and-revise step with and without oracle stop; report only the no-oracle number.

claim: Self-correction works where reliable external feedback exists (tests, code execution, tools) or the answer decomposes into verifiable parts.
agent_test: Gate S6 revisions on an executable check; compare to ungated revision at equal tokens.

claim: Error location is the bottleneck: models find the first wrong step poorly (GPT-4 52.87 on BIG-Bench Mistake) but fix well once the step is given. Update: on long reasoning-model chains the best critic reaches only F1 40.8 (DeltaBench), far below ProcessBench (o1-mini 87.9, QwQ 71.5, GPT-4o 61.9); a reasoning-model verifier with forced step checking (ThinkPRM) reaches F1 about 85 to 87 on OlympiadBench/OmniMath subsets.
agent_test: Test a separate step-locator pass (ProcessBench-style judge) feeding a backtrack, vs whole-answer review, at equal tokens.

claim: Models are blind to their own injected errors: the same error is missed in the model's own turn far more than when the user wrote it (64.5% average blind spot, 14 open non-reasoning models; Claude Sonnet 4 41.4%). Reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot, and appending Wait to a non-reasoning model nearly matches its reasoning sibling. On the model's own natural errors, showing them as external rescues only 4.3% to 10.8%.
agent_test: Present own prior step as if written by another party (role reframe) and compare error catch rate.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy problems: after the first correct solution later rounds add little (over 92% of cases first round correct; 1,953% more tokens on '2+3').
agent_test: Add a stop-after-first-verified-answer rule on easy items; measure tokens saved at equal accuracy.

claim: Reasoning models also underthink: wrong answers have 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches; a switch penalty (TIP) lifts AIME24 Pass@1 for QwQ 38.3 to 44.1. All rows come from one paper.
agent_test: Require a stated reason and a minimum probe depth before abandoning a line; compare with free switching.

claim: Shorter sampled chains are more often correct for the same question; parallel sampling beats extended sequential thinking at fixed budget (shortest up to 34.5% better than longest; parallel up to 22% at 16K).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare k short parallel runs vs one long run with 'Wait' extensions.

claim: Reasoning models encode whether an intermediate answer is correct but do not use it; a probe supports early exit (24% fewer tokens, accuracy 88.2% kept at threshold 0.85). Needs open-weight access.
agent_test: Not testable on a closed-API agent; use verbalised confidence as a weak proxy and calibrate against outcomes.

claim: The model's written reasoning is an unreliable monitoring signal: hints used are verbalised under 20% of the time (faithfulness 25% Claude 3.7 Sonnet, 39% R1).
schema_part: G (do not trust trace as evidence)
agent_test: Plant a hint, check whether S6 monitoring catches its use from the trace alone.

claim: Wait-style budget forcing helps modestly then flattens (s1-32B AIME24 50.0 to 56.7 with Wait x4; MATH500 flat; s1.1 no AIME24 gain) and may reflect variance rather than better reasoning.
agent_test: Sweep number of forced re-checks at equal total tokens; compare against matched extra samples plus vote.

claim: Reflection words ('aha') already occur in base models and do not correlate with accuracy; reflection ability appears in pretraining.
agent_test: Measure accuracy conditional on reflection phrases in own traces; do not use phrase counts as a progress signal.

claim: Four cognitive behaviours (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining) in a base model predict RL gains; priming with them, even with wrong answers, matters more than correctness (Countdown only).
agent_test: Seed prompt exemplars with these behaviours vs neutral filler at equal tokens.

claim: Search with explicit evaluation and backtracking is a strong external control layer (Game of 24, GPT-4: CoT 4%, ToT b=1 45%, b=5 74%).
agent_test: Compare ToT-style search vs CoT plus self-consistency at equal tokens on 24-type puzzles.

claim: Skill-labelled exemplar retrieval (metacognitive knowledge) raises MATH accuracy (GPT-4: 53.88 vs complex CoT 50.30, plain CoT 42.2) and GSM8K 93.00 to 94.31; random exemplars give none.
agent_test: Skill-named retrieval vs topic retrieval at equal prompt length.

claim: Reflexion-style verbal memory after a failed trial helps when the signal is reliable (ALFWorld 130/134 in 12 trials; HumanEval 91.0), triggered by a hand-written stuck rule (same action more than 3 cycles or more than 30 actions).
agent_test: Port the stuck rule (repeat count, step cap) to a maths agent; compare with no trigger at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models beat plain models only at medium complexity; the claimed collapse at high complexity is partly artifact (token limits, impossible instances).
agent_test: Re-run with output cap and solvability checked before concluding a give-up rule is needed.

claim: Human evidence that metacognitive instruction improves maths is thin: a 12-week grade 7 programme gave modest gains (regular N=22: 4.73 to 6.00; advanced N=34: 6.74 to 8.38, ceiling); calibration in grades 5-8 predicts later arithmetic growth (beta .269, N about 190). Later meta-analysis: self-regulated learning training, average d 0.69 across 84 primary and secondary studies (357 effects), higher in maths than reading (Dignath and Buettner 2008, abstract only).
agent_test: No direct test; treat human training effects as weak support for S6 design.

claim: A problem-solving course shifted novice problem perception toward deep structure (test mean 21 to 73 vs 14 to 24 control; N=19).
agent_test: Compare structure-first problem sort against surface read before choosing approach.

claim: Stable-answer or transition-point early exit shortens current open reasoning chains with no accuracy loss: DEER (R1-Distill-7B AIME24 41.7 to 49.2 with 13,765 to 9,839 tokens; MATH-500 87.4 to 89.8 with 3,858 to 2,143), Certaindex up to 50% compute saved, answer convergence at about 60% of steps. A stable wrong answer is not caught.
agent_test: Probe the trial answer at each Wait or at fixed intervals; stop when it repeats; ablate against no trigger at equal tokens on AIME-level items.

claim: A hand-written trigger on a progress signal (trial-answer confidence at a Wait, or lowest-group token confidence) beats no trigger on tokens and holds accuracy on competition maths with open 2025 models (DeepConf-low saves 43% to 79% tokens vs majority; DEER). No paper tests a repeated-step or step-cap stall rule against no trigger at equal tokens; Reflexion's rule (same action over 3 cycles or over 30 actions) was tested only in non-maths environments.
agent_test: Run repeated-step stall rule vs DEER-style probe vs none at equal tokens on MATH/AIME items.

claim: Verbalised confidence from reasoning models is better calibrated later in the chain and than in non-reasoning twins (33 of 36 settings), but nobody has tested it as a stop or switch signal on maths; token-probability confidence works as an abandon signal but is wrong on confident-but-wrong traces.
agent_test: Log verbalised confidence at each probe; measure AUROC for end-of-chain correctness; use only after the midpoint.

claim: Error location without ground truth stays hard: best critic on long reasoning chains F1 40.8 (DeltaBench) and self-critique 36% worse than critique of another model; a plain reasoning-model judge produces invalid output in up to 55% of cases (R1-1.5B) while a fine-tuned verifier with forced step checks reaches F1 about 87 on ProcessBench subsets.
agent_test: Use a separate step-checking pass with enforced output format; compare against tool check and disagreement of two samples.

claim: Extending thinking with Wait does not beat the same tokens spent on parallel samples with voting for small open reasoning models (parallel +10.1 vs Wait minus 11.8 at 16K on GSM8K R1-1.5B; short-3@k beats majority@k by 2 to 4 points). Wait-suppression (NoWait) cuts 27% to 51% of tokens without accuracy loss. No test exists on 2026 frontier models.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare k parallel samples with vote vs 1 chain with 0, 1, 2, 4 forced rechecks on a current model.

claim: Difficulty changes what the trace does: on easy puzzle items correct answers appear early and later exploration adds errors; on hard items models fixate on an early wrong answer. NoThinking matches full thinking on easy MATH levels 1 to 3. The gate is learned (AdaptThink) or analytic; a hand-written easy/hard gate on stop and switch rules is untested.
agent_test: Gate stop-after-first-verified on estimated easy items and force a switch after fixation on hard ones; compare to ungated rules.

claim: Self-judgement is biased toward own output: models recognise their own text (GPT-4 73.5%), self-refine amplifies self-bias, and showing own errors as another's rescues only a small share of natural errors. A role reframe is therefore weak insurance; an independent second sample or tool check is stronger.
schema_part: G (do not trust own progress claim)
agent_test: Compare reframe vs independent-sample check on the model's own natural errors in maths.
